title: HPC with Enhanced User Separation
problem: User-modified HPC software is rarely built with security in mind, creating risks in shared systems. Systems require enforcement of separation across processes, filesystem access, network traffic, and accelerators to prevent interference between users.
motivation: Shared HPC systems must support diverse research workflows while maintaining strong isolation guarantees to prevent security breaches and resource interference between users.
method: The system prevents users from interfering with each other by enforcing separation at four levels: isolating their running programs (processes), controlling which files they can access, blocking their network traffic from crossing, and restricting their access to hardware accelerators (like GPUs). Because all four barriers work together, each user sees only their own work and cannot access or affect what others are doing, even though they're all using the same physical hardware.
key_novelty: The key contribution is coordinating user separation across all four areas—processes, filesystem, network, and accelerators—to create strong isolation between users on shared HPC hardware.
contributions: Process isolation enforcement for HPC workloads
Filesystem access control and isolation techniques
